newsitem.title: USA: MCA/Viacom trial to resume Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: MCA/Viacom trial to resume Wednesday.

text.p: The trial in a partnership dispute between the MCA Inc affiliate of Seagram Co Ltd and Viacom Inc will resume Wednesday at 1300 EST/1800 GMT.

It is being interrupted for a day and a half because Vice Chancellor Myron Steele has a scheduling conflict. A source close to the case told Reuters that there are no settlement talks between the parties at this time.
MCA is seeking a court order that could force Viacom to sell its share of the USA Networks partnership to MCA at the low end of a valuation range.
In a countersuit, Viacom contends that the partnership is working fine and alleges that MCA has violated antitrust law and breached a contract with Viacom.
The trial, which began in the Delaware Chancery Court on Oct 15, was delayed Oct 22 for four days while the two sides tried unsuccessfully to negotiate a settlement.

Seagram chief executive Edgar Bronfman Jr. and Viacom chairman Sumner Redstone have testified differently about whether there was an agreement to exempt Viacom's MTV networks from litigation for alleged violation of the partnership's non-compete agreement.
The evidence-taking part of the trial is expected to end this week or early next week with testimony from Viacom executives and an anti-trust expert.

Instead of closing arguments in the courtroom, both sides will summarize their legal arguments in post-trial briefs. The briefing could be followed by oral arguments. A source told Reuters that it is possible but not likely that Steele would have a decision by year-end.
